question: Should the operator close the review for filter train M2?

claims.A: M2 passed the April pressure test.
claims.B: A bypass on M2 received a flow alarm at 09:10.
claims.C: M2 was serviced that morning.

sources.S1: control historian records a flow alarm on M2 bypass at 09:10.
sources.S2: shift sign-off says the site used filter train M1 all morning and no service was performed on M2.
sources.S3: maintenance chat says, 'M2 passed pressure from what I heard'. It has no instrument reading and was sent before the test team handed over results.

support.S4: metrology laboratory reports the witnessed M2 April pressure test met the pass standard at 14:05. It is independent of the chat sender.

retract.S4: metrology laboratory reports the witnessed M2 April pressure test fell below the pass standard at 14:05. It is independent of the chat sender.

question: Can stores release a pallet to the customer?

claims.A: Pallet H17 remained within its agreed temperature range during road transit.
claims.B: H17 arrived without any intact security seal.
claims.C: H17 checked in at the depot at 16:40.

sources.S1: gate scan records pallet H17 checked in at 16:40.
sources.S2: receiving note says H17 had two intact security seals.
sources.S3: carrier says the route normally stays cold and assumes H17 met its temperature requirement. The trailer air logger does not measure this pallet.

support.S4: the independent pallet-mounted logger shows H17 stayed within its agreed limits for the entire road transit.

retract.S4: the independent pallet-mounted logger records H17 exceeding its agreed upper limit for an hour during road transit.

question: Can the facilities team mark the room ready for an evening booking?

claims.A: Room F had an evening booking at 19:00.
claims.B: The replacement microphone worked in Room F at the post-repair test.
claims.C: The Room F wall plate was intact at 15:00.

sources.S1: venue calendar records Room F booked for 19:00.
sources.S2: technician photographed a cracked wall plate in Room F at 15:00.
sources.S3: supplier receipt confirms the new microphone powered on before shipment. A venue coordinator writes that it likely works in Room F.

support.S4: the independent evening crew's signed Room F post-repair test records sound captured cleanly from the replacement microphone.

retract.S4: the independent evening crew's signed Room F post-repair test records no captured signal from the replacement microphone.

question: Can the buyer close its pre-award eligibility check?

claims.A: Vale submitted a bid on lot 3.
claims.B: Vendor Vale held the required liability policy on 1 July.
claims.C: The Vale bid was submitted before the deadline.

sources.S1: tender portal sealed and timestamped the Vale bid 42 minutes before the deadline.
sources.S2: Vale circulated a draft quote saying its coverage should start 1 July. It is labelled conditional on payment and contains no binding notice.
sources.S3: tender portal shows Vale bid on lot 2 only.

support.S4: the insurer, independent of the vendor, confirms the policy was bound and active on 1 July.

retract.S4: the insurer, independent of the vendor, confirms no active policy covered Vale on 1 July.

question: Which catalogue claims can go into the public entry?

claims.A: The archive acquired the map case in 1962.
claims.B: The map has no fold on its western edge.
claims.C: The original map plate was engraved in 1893.

sources.S1: accession book records the map case acquired in 1962.
sources.S2: an undated loose label in the case says 'engraving probably 1893'. Neighbouring maps use duplicate cases. No plate impression was checked.
sources.S3: a condition report locates a fold on the western edge.

support.S4: independent paper conservators inspected the original map plate and authenticated its engraved date of 1893.

retract.S4: independent paper conservators inspected the original map plate and authenticated its engraved date of 1895.

question: Can the incident lead close a postal service ticket?

claims.A: The ticket intake had zero original delivery complaints.
claims.B: The print room released 140 replacement issues on Monday.
claims.C: All 140 replacement issues were delivered on Tuesday.

sources.S1: printer dispatch manifest records 140 replacement issues released on Monday.
sources.S2: coordinator marks 'delivery complete' when the van departs and tells the desk the replacements should all arrive Tuesday.
sources.S3: ticket intake lists 37 original delivery complaints before the replacements.

support.S4: an independent postal receipt reconciliation shows 140 of 140 individual replacement issues delivered on Tuesday.

retract.S4: an independent postal receipt reconciliation shows 136 delivered Tuesday and the final four delivered Wednesday.

question: Can the plant send bench W8 to assembly?

claims.A: Bench W8 withstood a 600 N load in the batch acceptance test.
claims.B: Bench W8 came from production lot L9.
claims.C: Bench W8 had only three fittings torqued before acceptance.

sources.S1: torque record lists four fittings torqued before acceptance.
sources.S2: production traveller assigns bench W8 to lot L9 by serial number.
sources.S3: a photograph shows 600 N on a controller setpoint. The serial sticker is cropped out and the measured load is absent.

support.S4: a separate quality rig record identifies W8 and records a completed, passing 600 N acceptance test.

retract.S4: a separate quality rig record identifies W8 and records collapse at 575 N in the acceptance test.

question: Can the project report the backup trial as complete?

claims.A: The battery supplied emergency loads continuously for 60 minutes on Thursday.
claims.B: The diesel generator was connected for the trial.
claims.C: The trial started on Thursday at 08:00.

sources.S1: generator log shows the diesel generator was disconnected for the trial.
sources.S2: trial sign-in records the start Thursday at 08:00.
sources.S3: mobile dashboard reports a battery runtime estimate of 62 minutes. An email calls the trial a success based on that estimate.

support.S4: independent inline power logger records the battery supplying the emergency loads without interruption for the first 60 minutes Thursday.

retract.S4: independent inline power logger records the battery losing emergency load after 43 minutes Thursday.

question: Can the coordinator report that room changes reached participants?

claims.A: The workshop moved from Room 1 to Room 4.
claims.B: Every registered attendee received the change notice before noon.
claims.C: The workshop had 20 registered attendees.

sources.S1: registration ledger records 18 registered attendees.
sources.S2: booking ledger records the workshop move from Room 1 to Room 4.
sources.S3: email server accepted 18 sends and the front desk assumes receipt. The send report excludes delivery and bounce status.

support.S4: independent mailbox audit matches all 18 registered addresses to a delivered room change notice before noon.

retract.S4: independent mailbox audit finds two registered addresses first received the notice after noon.

question: Which bridge incident claims can be published in the log?

claims.A: The specified ferry was hull number 29.
claims.B: The 12:10 ferry crossed before traffic reopened.
claims.C: The ferry left its dock at 12:10.

sources.S1: a draft dispatch summary marks crossing first then road opening, but explicitly combines entries from unsynchronised clocks.
sources.S2: dock departure log records the specified ferry leaving at 12:10.
sources.S3: mechanical register assigns the ferry hull number 42.

support.S4: an independent clock-aligned video reconciliation shows the hull-42 crossing ended at 12:19 and traffic reopened at 12:24.

retract.S4: an independent clock-aligned video reconciliation shows traffic reopened at 12:14 and the hull-42 crossing ended at 12:19.

question: Can the archive publish a channel specification?

claims.A: The archive ingested a digital file from session K.
claims.B: The archive stored one verified copy.
claims.C: The master from session K is stereo.

sources.S1: the emailed file name includes 'stereo' but the sender says the same label was reused from two previous recordings.
sources.S2: digital intake records a file from session K ingested.
sources.S3: preservation log says the archive stored three verified copies.

support.S4: conservator independently inspects the labelled session K master and measures distinct left/right audio channels.

retract.S4: conservator independently inspects the labelled session K master and finds a single mono audio channel.

question: Can the stock manager order jars against a shipment record?

claims.A: The G11 pallet was wet on arrival.
claims.B: G11 arrived with six cartons.
claims.C: Shipment G11 contained at least 96 saleable jars at arrival.

sources.S1: the packing plan specifies 16 jars per carton. Staff did not count or inspect the jars and described 96 as the expected saleable count.
sources.S2: courier unloading receipt confirms six G11 cartons arrived.
sources.S3: pallet inspection confirms the pallet was dry on arrival.

support.S4: an independent sealed-camera count and inspection at arrival confirms 96 saleable jars in G11.

retract.S4: an independent sealed-camera count and inspection at arrival confirms 92 saleable jars and four broken ones in G11.

question: Should the superintendent release the concrete delivery invoice?

claims.A: Truck Z7 was within tolerance for slump at discharge.
claims.B: Truck Z7 arrived before 07:30.
claims.C: The delivery docket lists mix grade M20 for Z7.

sources.S1: delivery docket records mix grade M30 for Z7.
sources.S2: the dispatch desk logged an in-range reading at batching; the foreman expects the result to carry over to discharge.
sources.S3: gate record places truck Z7 onsite at 07:14.

support.S4: an independent field lab's signed slump test for Z7 at discharge falls within the applicable tolerance.

retract.S4: an independent field lab's signed slump test for Z7 at discharge falls outside the applicable tolerance.

question: Can lands staff certify the pump telemetry report?

claims.A: Pump P9 reached at least 40 litres per minute on its first test.
claims.B: P9 had a 3-inch intake installed on the test bench.
claims.C: Technicians powered P9 on Wednesday.

sources.S1: the bench register specifies a 2-inch intake installed.
sources.S2: maintenance engineer circulated a design curve showing 43 litres per minute with a similar intake and wrote that 40 seemed safe.
sources.S3: bench activation register confirms P9 powered on Wednesday.

support.S4: an independent calibrated meter records P9 at 43 litres per minute during its first test.

retract.S4: an independent calibrated meter records P9 never exceeding 37 litres per minute during its first test.

question: Can the venue confirm that linen met the banquet checklist?

claims.A: Three event linen kits were issued.
claims.B: The event linen kits included at least one spare cloth each.
claims.C: The linen kits were issued for booking E31.

sources.S1: issue register identifies the banquet as booking E77.
sources.S2: the warehouse's usual packing checklist calls for a spare cloth; the event boxes were packed during a rush and the checklist was unsigned.
sources.S3: issue register records three event linen kits issued.

support.S4: a separate venue inventory at the time of issue verified one or more spare cloths in every event linen kit.

retract.S4: a separate venue inventory at the time of issue verified kit 2 contained no spare cloth.

question: Can the review board close the leak-testing row for V31?

claims.A: V31 was in lot R8.
claims.B: Valve V31 passed the helium leak test at 3 bar.
claims.C: V31 underwent a nitrogen test.

sources.S1: a QA email refers to a 3-bar test on V31 and assumes it was helium. The archived gas field is blank.
sources.S2: incoming inspection places V31 in lot R6.
sources.S3: rig output records a completed nitrogen test on V31.

support.S4: an independently archived helium rig result records a passing 3-bar test on V31.

retract.S4: an independently archived helium rig result records a failing 3-bar test on V31.

question: Can the archivist sign off on the map backup?

claims.A: Snapshot M3 was created at 23:05.
claims.B: Snapshot M3 was written on volume West.
claims.C: Backup snapshot M3 includes the final parcel boundary layer.

sources.S1: author marked the final layer as ready before 23:05, but the transfer queue was not checked.
sources.S2: storage receipt identifies it as snapshot M3 on volume East.
sources.S3: backup job log timestamps snapshot M3 at 23:05.

support.S4: an independent restoration audit confirms the final parcel boundary layer hash exists in recovered M3.

retract.S4: an independent restoration audit confirms recovered M3 contains only the predecessor layer hash and no final parcel boundary layer.

question: Can extension staff cite a field sample as meeting the wetness target?

claims.A: Plot W was in the centre of the block.
claims.B: Plot W was sampled at noon.
claims.C: Plot W was below the moisture target when sampled at noon.

sources.S1: a plot supervisor saw a dry upper surface and reported likely low moisture, but the sampling procedure measures deeper soil.
sources.S2: field map marks W as the outside plot.
sources.S3: signed collection tag records Plot W sampled at noon.

support.S4: an independent gravimetric assay of the noon Plot W sample measures moisture below the target.

retract.S4: an independent gravimetric assay of the noon Plot W sample measures moisture above the target.

question: Can the dispatcher release the amended loading summary?

claims.A: Container C74 passed its dockside seal integrity check.
claims.B: The loading crane lifted C74 at 06:25.
claims.C: C74 is a standard-height container.

sources.S1: crane lift log records container C74 lifted at 06:25.
sources.S2: container register identifies high-cube size.
sources.S3: an upstream driver inspection showed an intact seal on arrival. A rough lift and temporary hold occurred before the dockside check.

support.S4: the separate dockside seal inspection, after the lift, reports C74's seal passed the integrity check.

retract.S4: the separate dockside seal inspection, after the lift, reports C74's seal failed the integrity check.

question: Can the clerk mark installation complete for the northern signs?

claims.A: The signs were mounted facing the paths on opening day.
claims.B: The signs were made of wood.
claims.C: The signs were delivered on Thursday.

sources.S1: signed carrier slip records Thursday delivery.
sources.S2: inventory lists four aluminium signs.
sources.S3: the foreman's work order describes the intended orientation and was checked off without requiring an orientation photograph.

support.S4: an independent time-stamped opening-day survey shows all four signs facing the paths.

retract.S4: an independent time-stamped opening-day survey shows one of the four signs facing away from the path.

question: Can a customer representative confirm compliance for lot K19?

claims.A: The workshop bought lot K19 in February.
claims.B: Lot K19 met its minimum wash-fastness rating on receipt.
claims.C: Lot K19 was ordered as red silk.

sources.S1: signed purchase record places the lot K19 purchase in February.
sources.S2: the purchase record describes the order as grey cotton.
sources.S3: a vendor's general brochure reports this product family usually meets the minimum rating. It contains no lot K19 test result.

support.S4: independent laboratory report on a retained receipt sample places K19 at or above the specified wash-fastness minimum.

retract.S4: independent laboratory report on a retained receipt sample places K19 below the specified wash-fastness minimum.

question: Can operations close the sign-off for the west entrance count?

claims.A: West entrance had zero ticket scans in the first minute.
claims.B: At least six ushers were present at the west entrance at 09:00.
claims.C: West entrance opened at 09:00.

sources.S1: duty log records West entrance opened at 09:00.
sources.S2: a roster assigns six ushers to the entrance but has no sign-in record. The shift coordinator assumes all attended.
sources.S3: gate log records eight ticket scans in the first minute.

support.S4: an independent opening-time photograph and vest-code roster verify six ushers at West entrance at 09:00.

retract.S4: an independent opening-time photograph and vest-code roster verify four ushers at West entrance at 09:00.

question: What claims can the archivist put in the tape catalogue?

claims.A: Staff digitised the master tape on Friday.
claims.B: The original tape casing is labelled programme SR-63.
claims.C: The master tape contains more than 30 minutes of programme audio.

sources.S1: transfer log records the master tape digitised Friday.
sources.S2: the programme grid allocates 35 minutes. Engineers routinely removed news and announcements from masters, so the slot is only an estimate.
sources.S3: tape casing is labelled programme SR-36 by the original studio.

support.S4: independent digital preservation report distinguishes programme audio from silence and assigns the master 32 minutes of programme audio.

retract.S4: independent digital preservation report distinguishes programme audio from silence and assigns the master 28 minutes of programme audio.

question: Can inventory certify the dispatch packing bill?

claims.A: Box J weighed 3.2 kg with packaging.
claims.B: Box J was sent to the second workshop.
claims.C: Box J contained the full replacement hinge kit at dispatch.

sources.S1: dispatch registry identifies the second workshop as the recipient of J.
sources.S2: a matching kit typically weighs 1.4 kg when packed. Miscellaneous loose hardware was also pooled on the packing table.
sources.S3: dispatch registry records J weighed 1.4 kg with packaging.

support.S4: independent opening inventory confirms all specified replacement hinge parts in J, with dispatch seal unbroken on arrival.

retract.S4: independent opening inventory confirms two specified hinge parts missing from J, with dispatch seal unbroken on arrival.
